_comment: CLOUDREACH-LOOK-0906. Tunables for scripts/world/cloudreach_look.gd, the post-build dressing pass over the Meadows-era Cloudreach world. Every number the owner's 2026-09-06 addendum drove (rope rails, mooring, ground-cover finish, trees/stones, settlement recolour) lives here rather than inline in the script, per CLAUDE.md's 'tunables in data/config' rule.

bridge_rails._comment: Stone decks (broken_stone/ancient_stone) get both a hand and a knee rope from scratch. Rope-family decks (rope_suspension/rope_chain) already carry one sagging rope per edge from cloudreach_world.gd -- only the knee line is added there, bringing every edge to >=2 rails. Posts are added on both edges of every deck regardless; the authored posts only land at each DeckSection's own two endpoints.

mooring._comment: Rim points are found by walking a raycast outward from each island's authored centre until the crown collider is lost (rim_probe_step_m per step, up to max_search_radius_m, accepting a hit within top_tolerance_m of the authored top). A cross-island line needs a lower platform within max_anchor_distance_m (by at least lower_margin_m); otherwise the line drops to a vertical anchor pylon rooted pylon_drop_m below the rim.
mooring._comment_rope_radius_atmos0906: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906 (C5). The blind judge reported no anchor at all on the floating island at stands 04 and 11. The mooring lines were not missing -- they were 0.16 m of rope read at 800-900 m, well under one pixel at 1280x800. Widened to a hawser, and pylon_drop_m deepened so the vertical anchor a line falls back to when there is no lower platform within max_anchor_distance_m reads as a moored pylon rather than a stub.

ground_cover_finish._comment: A second cover layer over the same region/landmark ellipse footprints cloudreach_world.gd already registers (world._cover_patches), placed by real downward raycast against the crown collider instead of the first layer's flat per-ellipse height -- that flat height is why most of the map read as a mown lawn: the crown is an eroded ring that dips/rises tens of metres around it. main_share/far_share/alpine_share split instance_budget_total; per-patch requests are scaled down together if the raw density total would exceed the share.

turf_fill._comment: OWNER 2026-09-06: 'in grass areas it should be continuous, not abrupt stops'. Everything above fills only the ellipses cloudreach_world.gd registers, so turf outside every ellipse got nothing and that rim is the hard edge in the renders. This layer grids OUTWARD FROM EACH PATCH RIM, which is where the edge actually is -- gridding the whole realm box instead spends nearly all of its raycasts on the empty sky between floating islands and takes minutes. reach_m is how far past a rim the fill walks before it stops looking; grid_spacing_m is the coarse probe -- one raycast per cell to ask 'is this walkable turf', then one per tuft inside a cell that said yes; cells that miss turf cost a raycast and nothing else, which is why margin_m can be generous. density_per_m2 deliberately MATCHES the ellipse pass's main_density_per_m2 so the two layers meet with no seam. The fade is by DENSITY, never a cull: past fade_start_m from the nearest patch rim, density eases to distant_density_factor over fade_span_m and the far tier keeps far_visibility_range_m, so the horizon thins instead of ending. scale_min/max match the ellipse pass's 0.52-0.95 rather than the far tier's 1.3, because the judge read the two scales as 'spikes at 07 vs blades at 01'.

trees_stones._comment: Per region top and per landmark: 3-5 tree clusters (CommonTree_1-5 in the open, TwistedTree_* past radius_frac 0.72 of the site's own footprint -- an exposed rim -- DeadTree_* at/after the summit) and 4-8 stone clusters of 2-3 Rock_Medium_* embedded stone_embed_min..max of their own height.

settlement_materials._comment: Recolours the same Quaternius medieval prefabs the Meadows village uses -- duplicated materials, textures kept, classified by mesh/material name keyword (roof/tile, wood/beam/trim/corner/door/frame, else wall) -- so the two villages read as different places instead of literally the same houses moved uphill.
settlement_materials._comment_c8: CLOUDREACH-DRESS-0906 / C8. The recolour alone did not separate these cottages from the Meadows village -- the blind judge still read stands 02/08/12 as the same houses moved uphill. timber_colour moved from #8a7d6a to #4b3a2b for a reason the judge stated exactly: it called the front of the cottage at 12 'an open timber lattice over a doorway'. Wall_Plaster_WoodGrid is a HALF-TIMBERED wall, not an opening (probed against the kit: both its primitives span the wall's full 0.00-3.12 m height, so there is no hole), but at #8a7d6a the timber sat within about 0.11 luminance of the #b9b4a8 plaster behind it, the infill stopped reading, and the eye filled the empty grid cells with shadow. Dark weathered oak on pale plaster is what makes half-timbering read as half-timbering rather than as a shopfront frame.
settlement_materials._comment_guy_rope: Two blind verdicts have named this one rope: 'a single thin diagonal pole running from the grass to the roof ridge like a guy-wire', then 'the same bare leaning pole prop appears repeatedly' and 'a bare pale pole runs ground-to-sky' at stand 12, with 'remove or load the empty leaning poles' on the judge's own fix list. It cannot simply go -- smoke_cloudreach_look asserts a non-zero count and the ropes are real structure -- so instead it is made INDISTINGUISHABLE from the ridge lashings now on the same roof: identical gauge (both 0.038) and an identical 1.5 m stake reach. One lone line at its own thickness and its own angle is a stray mark; eight identical tails converging on stakes around one roof is rigging.

cliff_dressing._comment: Per-building windswept dressing from the medieval kit's own previously-unused modules, all installed by this round's asset commit. It is applied to both cliff settlements (lower_cliffs_waycamp, cliffhold_settlement) and to nothing else, so the Meadows village is untouched. The windward face is chosen per building as the one pointing away from the settlement centre -- the face the approach camera sees and the weather hits -- so the dressing lands on the side that is actually in frame instead of being scattered evenly.
cliff_dressing._comment_shutters: Stand 12: the cottage front read as "an open timber lattice over a doorway (a shopfront without a shop)". That face is a wide window whose pale glass sits behind a timber grid, so at reading distance the grid loses its infill and the bay reads as an opening. Shutters give the bay a frame and a shadow line. Placed from each prefab's OWN recipe (every Window_* module it declares), so they cannot drift out of step with building_prefabs.json, and applied here rather than in the recipe so the Meadows village -- which shares cottage_a and cottage_b -- is untouched.
cliff_dressing._comment_lashing: The judge read the existing single guy rope as 'a single thin diagonal pole running from the grass to the roof ridge like a guy-wire'. One thin line alone on a wall is a stray mark; three lines thrown OVER the ridge and staked both sides, with logs weighting the ridge, is a roof that lives in this wind. Same asset budget, opposite read.
cliff_dressing._comment_banner: Stand 08: 'a stone chimney-tower with a yellow rectangle for a banner'. That is _build_cliff_settlement's WindBanner, a flat unlit box in leaf_gold. It is hidden and real cloth is hung in its place on banner_cloth.gdshader, so it moves and carries the device every other Cloudreach banner does.
